clue.text: Abandon power after party seizes rule

indicators.note: the letter for power comes after the party-and-rule unit
the party word grabs and holds the letter for rule inside itself

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A political party grabs control and then gives up power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizes' puts R inside DO; 'after' sets P behind that.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan or a friend is to abandon it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Up for a bit of rumpy-pumpy with boyfriend (no saint)

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word rumpy-pumpy is used, its opening letter
no saint means the abbreviation for saint is removed from the boyfriend word

parts.note: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend

explanation.surface: Someone eager for a bit of romance with a boyfriend who is no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: A steady is a regular partner; 'no' strips the saint from it, and 'a bit of' points to the opening letter of the bedroom slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up for something means being willing and prepared to do it, the same as prepared.

clue.text: One predicts the changes following support

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the support word

parts.note: a prop is something that supports

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the word the are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecaster foresees the changes that follow some support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' looks like a noun about the future but is the instruction to rearrange 'the'; 'following' puts that after the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer or oracle foretells the future, so is one who predicts.

clue.text: Insurance company's extremely reduced

indicators.note: reduced means the word for extremely is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: An insurance company has drastically cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' reads as cost-cutting but means the word for 'extremely' loses its tail; the apostrophe-s is just 'is' linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance cover is the protection a policy provides, so the two words are used as synonyms.

clue.text: Dog with favourite food around street? Edge of street in America

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the favourite food word goes around the street abbreviation

parts.note: a bone is a dog's proverbial favourite food

explanation.surface: A dog with its favourite treat wandering around the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the bone round the street abbreviation. The British spelling of the answer begins with a K: kerbstone.
explanation.definitionFit: In American spelling the stone edging of a pavement is a curbstone, the US form of kerbstone.

clue.text: Rocky cove vandals ruin in North American location

indicators.note: rocky means shaky or unsteady, so the letters of cove vandals ruin are jumbled

explanation.surface: Vandals wreck a rocky cove somewhere in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like it describes the cove but signals rearranging all fifteen letters of 'cove vandals ruin'.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island off the coast of British Columbia, Canada, is a place in North America.

clue.text: Lecturer and I leaving to take pressure off old magistrate

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for lecturer and I depart from the word for easing pressure

parts.note: to relieve is to ease or take pressure off

explanation.surface: A lecturer and I go off to relieve the strain on an old official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L and I out of RELIEVE. A reeve was a local official or magistrate in medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a chief officer or magistrate of a town or district in old England.

clue.text: Maintain H is at front of 'historic'

indicators.note: the letter H is placed in front of the word for historic

parts.note: old means historic or of the past

explanation.surface: An insistence that the letter H belongs at the front of 'historic'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the old debate over 'a historic' or 'an historic', but 'historic' is just a synonym for OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a view or a position is to maintain it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Church item showing a couple of Saints breaking open wine

indicators.note: the a and two saints break into the middle of the wine word

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
S is the abbreviation for saint, so two saints give SS

explanation.surface: A church item showing two saints cracking open a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking open' splits the German wine after its first letter to let the saints in. Hock is a British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion for kneeling on in church pews is a classic piece of church furniture.

clue.text: I have stone brought in to secure animals

indicators.note: the I-have and stone pieces are brought into the word for secure

parts.note: to lock is to secure
I've is the contraction of I have
ST is the abbreviation for the weight stone

explanation.surface: Someone has had stone delivered to build a pen securing their animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in to' puts IVEST inside LOCK, after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm animals collectively, such as cattle and sheep, are the farm's livestock.

clue.text: Unenviable working with tiros, requiring a lot of effort

indicators.note: working means the letters are being reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An unenviable job alongside beginners which takes a great deal of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges UNENVIABLE plus TIROS. A tiro is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A task needing much work or manpower is described as heavy on toil, using lots of human effort.

clue.text: Extremes of military tech are fiction

indicators.note: the extremes of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Stories about extreme military technology are just made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes of' takes M and Y from 'military' and T and H from 'tech'.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a made-up story, so a piece of fiction or untruth.

clue.text: Granary others rebuilt beside river

indicators.note: the river is placed beside the rearranged letters
rebuilt means the letters of others are reassembled differently

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Other people rebuilt a granary next to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns OTHERS into STOREH, set beside OUSE, a river in Yorkshire and also in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a building where grain is stored, a kind of warehouse for crops.

clue.text: At all events, a row developed about Hungary not Norway

indicators.note: developed and about both suggest change, so the combined letters are rearranged
Hungary not Norway means one country letter stands where the other was

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: At sporting events a row breaks out involving Hungary rather than Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At all events' reads as one phrase, but 'events' is fodder. Swapping N for H in EVENTS gives EVEHTS; 'developed about' rearranges that with A ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Used for emphasis after a negative, as in no doubt of any kind, the word means at all.

clue.text: Unimaginative note journalist observed going round

indicators.note: the journalist and observed pieces together go round the note letter

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
eyed means watched or observed

explanation.surface: A dull note: a journalist was seen doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' applies to the journalist and 'observed' together, which surround the note abbreviation rather than either word alone doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed phrases are stale and overused, so lacking originality or imagination.

clue.text: Trainer finally ready with the fluid — to do this?

definitions.text: Trainer finally ready with the fluid — to do this?

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word trainer
fluid means not fixed, so the letters of ready and the flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainer at last has a drink ready for an athlete, to restore their fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'Trainer'; 'fluid' rearranges READY plus THE to EHYDRATE. As a whole, the clue describes a trainer with fluid ready for this.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer supplying fluid to an athlete is restoring lost water to the body.

clue.text: Be aware of return of policy advisor

indicators.note: return means the word for policy advisor is read backwards

parts.note: a wonk is a policy expert, a nerdy political advisor

explanation.surface: Someone is aware that a policy advisor has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns WONK back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to be aware of it or have knowledge of it.

clue.text: Boat's lower, having lost stern

indicators.note: a stern is the back of a boat, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to lower, rhyming with flower, is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: A boat is lower in the water having lost its stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'less high' but is the verb meaning frown, SCOWL; 'having lost stern' drops its last letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat, such as a barge used for cargo.

clue.text: Referee's intervention in game getting lot of support

indicators.note: the game word takes on the trimmed support word after it

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: a lot of the word means most of it, all but its last letter

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A referee steps into a game that is getting plenty of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in game' looks like part of the definition, but 'game' gives the card game and 'in' only links; 'lot of' keeps most of the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee intervenes in a match by blowing a whistle, so the signal stands for the intervention.

clue.text: Calamity: attention and hard question brought into perspective

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: the hard and question letters are brought inside the perspective word

parts.note: a take on something is a perspective or view
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A disaster: careful attention and a hard question put things in perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' puts HQU inside TAKE, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A major earthquake is a natural disaster, an example of a calamity.

clue.text: Republican bet on university getting upset about Republican

indicators.note: the reversed betting phrase goes about the Republican letter
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the betting phrase reads backwards

parts.note: to lay on a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A Republican bet on a university that turned against Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' reverses LAYON to NOYAL; 'about' puts R inside, after its N. The first 'Republican' means opposed to monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects monarchy is a republican, hence not royal or anti-royal.

clue.text: Small music labels, non-English, took stance, faring poorly

indicators.note: non- says the letter for English is taken away from the labels word

parts.note: indies are small independent record labels
posed means struck a pose or took a stance

explanation.surface: Small foreign record labels that struck an attitude are doing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Indie is short for an independent record label; 'non-' removes the English abbreviation from the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwell is in poor health, so faring poorly is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Cats turned up — a great many, but not all

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is read the other way round
not all of the word for a great many is used, its last letter goes

parts.note: a mass of things is a great many of them

explanation.surface: Cats turned up in huge numbers, though not every one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats turned up' reads as cats arriving; actually 'turned' reverses 'up' to PU, and 'but not all' trims MASS to MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumas are large wild cats of the Americas, also called cougars.

clue.text: Free entry to exhibition? Go on!

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Free admission to the exhibition? Go on then!
explanation.walkthrough: 'entry to' gives E from 'exhibition', after RID.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a fairground attraction is to go on it.

clue.text: Medic feeling sick will identify procedure

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
ill means unwell or feeling sick

explanation.surface: A doctor who feels unwell will work out the right course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a set routine or procedure, as in a fire drill.

clue.text: My assassin worked with style and an efficient approach

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: My hired killer operated with flair and efficient methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges MY ASSASSIN plus STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This discipline studies how an organisation's processes work to make them run more efficiently.

clue.text: Useless fish in Lake? On the contrary

indicators.note: in would put fish inside lake, but the reversal says the lake letter goes inside the fish
on the contrary flips the container relation so the lake sits within the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish in a lake is useless? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns 'fish in Lake' round: L goes inside IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or ineffective, as in idle threats, so of no use.

clue.text: Second appearance of previous answer? A sly move

parts.note: the previous answer is the solution to 25 Across, the clue just before

explanation.surface: A repeated answer, used a second time, is a sneaky trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25 Across is IDLE; S for second goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge along furtively is the sense; as a noun it is a furtive, sideways movement.

clue.text: Person of great purity weakly rejecting politician

indicators.note: rejecting means the politician letters are thrown out of the weak word

parts.note: limply means weakly
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A pure soul weakly turns down a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' removes MP from LIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The white flower is a traditional emblem of purity, so it can stand for a pure person.
